title: Black Garlic and Chive Compound Butter
description: Black garlic brings a mellow sweetness to a chive butter made to melt into a generous spoonful of hot gravy.
equipment: Parchment or two small lidded containers
16-cavity tablespoon portion tray or kitchen scale

ingredients.name: fresh chives
ingredients.note: Washed, dried well and cut into very fine pieces.

steps.title: Soften the butter
steps.text: Let {butter} soften just until pliable, usually 20–30 minutes depending on the kitchen. Cut it into cubes so it softens evenly.

steps.title: Smooth the black garlic
steps.text: Mash {garlic} with a small piece of the softened butter until evenly blended.

steps.title: Fold in the chives
steps.text: Work {chives} and the rest of the softened butter into the garlic mixture with a spatula. Mix gently to keep the portions dense.

steps.title: Portion and chill
steps.text: Divide the batch into sixteen equal portions, about a level tablespoon each, or weigh the finished batch and divide its weight by sixteen. Cover and chill for at least 30 minutes.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Whisk a portion off heat into hot, thickened mushroom or chicken gravy. Ladle the enriched gravy generously over the protein.

notes: Yield: About 1 cup. One serving is 1 tablespoon, or one sixteenth of the batch. Make ahead: Soften the butter only as long as needed. Prepare the portions a day ahead and keep covered and cold. Refrigerate within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Freeze covered portions for up to 2 months. The garlic is finely dispersed and will blend back into gravy. Fridge reheat: Whisk a cold portion into hot, already thickened gravy off heat until melted. For a leftover meal, first reheat the food and gravy to 165°F throughout. Freezer reheat: Thaw a portion covered in the refrigerator overnight and finish the hot gravy as above. Option A uses the full amount of black garlic. For gentler Option B, halve the puree and replace the missing volume with unsalted butter. Use unsalted plant-based butter for a dairy-free version. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/16 of recipe): 91 kcal, 0.2 g protein, 0.3 g total carbohydrate, 10.1 g fat, 0.0 g fiber, 2 mg sodium. The estimate covers the prepared condiment. Add separately served foods when totaling a meal.

steps.title: Fit the blade
steps.text: Use short pulses in a mini food processor for the mixing step. Scrape down twice. For butter, start softened; for mayonnaise, pulse just until combined.
